name: Wasa
sweep_summary: Wasa (wasa1244) is not in the catalog and the sweep turned up a single title-match: Kandybowicz & Torrence 2015 (ACAL 44, Cascadilla), which is open access and was fetched sources and read in full with). It is a syntax-prosody paper on Intonational-Phrase mapping of embedded clauses in Krachi and Wasa (L% boundary tone, pause, pitch reset on a two-tone H/L system); it contains no word-stress or accent-placement statement and its footnote 1 says the authors could not locate any written materials on Wasa. Relevance: prosody-but-not-word-stress; bears on catalog: no-catalog-record; acquisition priority: none. No first-hand word-stress statement for Wasa was read, so best_new_statement is found=false. This matches the earlier worldframe fullscan verdict for this item (NO-SOURCE-FOUND). the Glottolog langdoc CSV endpoint returned a generic dump rather than a Wasa-specific list, and Ethnologue returned 403. If a stress statement for Wasa is wanted, the nearest candidates would be Akan-cluster descriptions (e.g. Dolphyne 1988 on Twi-Fante sound systems and tone), which would be other-variety evidence, not Wasa-specific.

sources.citation: Kandybowicz, Jason & Harold Torrence (2015). The prosodic licensing of wh-in-situ: Evidence from Krachi and Wasa. In Ruth Kramer, Elizabeth C. Zsiga & One Tlale Boyer (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 44th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 146-157. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.quote: For Wasa, we use a modified (non-IPA) version of the Akan script, as we have been unable to locate materials written in the language. [fn. 1, p. 147] ... Comparable phonetic correlates of right edge ι marking (i.e. L%, pause, pitch reset) exist in Wasa. This is demonstrated below by way of a clause modified by a reason adjunct. In this construction, the lexically H-bearing C0 sɛ at the right edge of ι surfaces with a depressed/falling F0. Following the complementizer is a pause. The range of F0 values following the break is also reset. [sec. 4.4, p. 154]
sources.locator: fn. 1, p. 147 (transcription conventions); sec. 4.4 'Prosodic status of Wasa embedded complement clauses', pp. 154-155
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a syntax-prosody study of whether embedded complement clauses are mapped as Intonational Phrases (diagnosed by L% boundary tone on the H-toned complementizer, pause, and pitch reset); Wasa is handled as a two-tone (H/L) language with continuous F0 downdrift across clauses. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the text; there is no statement of word-level stress or accent placement, and no phonological sketch of the word. Footnote 1 records that the authors could locate no written materials on Wasa at all.
